messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Multiple GPU OOM-driven container restarts observed on cluster inference-prod-usw2. Threshold breach detected at ~03:05UTC for oom/container_restart. Auto-page sent. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/prefill-oom

alice.m: oncall responding. seeing a cluster-wide uptick in restarts and a couple of nodes showing repeated Xid GPU errors. pulling pod events and recent traces.

ben: quick snapshot: restart-rate went from ~0.2/min -> 3.8/min across inference-prod-usw2; tail shows prefill allocations spiking for some sessions. sample event: 
```
Event: Container killed due to OOMKilled (oom_reaper), reason="OOMKilled"\nStack: serving/prefill_manager.go:276 -> runtime/alloc/gpu_kv.go:142
```

raj: checking request logs. Looks like a single API key (tenant id: analytics-ingest-42) sent multiple long-prefill batches: 18k+ tokens each, often concurrently (10+). KV cache and prefix allocations exhaust GPU VRAM.

infra-bot: Nodes with issues: gnode-5c, gnode-5d. GPU memory fragmentation high; dmesg contains repeated NVRM Xid 31 and Xid 57 messages. spare-node pool depleted (0 available).

pager_sre: Paging: @alice.m @raj assigned. If impact > 5% of total requests escalate to infra lead.

alice.m: mitigation plan (immediate -> short -> longer):
* Immediate: enable route-level prefill truncation and turn on per-tenant prefill-rate limiting for offending API key.
* Short: deploy runtime canary reducing max_prefill_tokens to 4096 and enable cold-fallback for > 8k prefill.
* Short: temporarily disable streaming on heavy routes to reduce in-flight KV allocations.
* Medium: cordon/drain affected nodes, schedule reboot to clear GPU driver state.
* Longer: add tenant-level quotas + alerting for token flood patterns.
Applying step 1 now (route toggles + rate-limit).

support-leah: Customer update: support ticket opened for analytics-ingest-42; they saw ~4% error rate and retries; account manager looped in. Several other customers had transient 5xx spikes, total impacted ~1.8% of platform bytes.

raj: pushed a temporary per-key rate-limit to throttle long-prefill requests from analytics-ingest-42. Confirmed their concurrent long-prefill connections dropped from 12 -> 1.

ben: enabling runtime canary with reduced prefill window on 20% of traffic to observe regression: 
```
runtimectl set --cluster=inference-prod-usw2 --param=max_prefill_tokens=4096 --param=enable_cold_fallback=true --canary=20%
```

runtime-bot: Canary deployed to inference-prod-usw2 canary group. Monitoring latency/quality deltas.

alice.m: also toggled `streaming.enabled=false` for /v1/chat-heavy (will reduce concurrency pressure). commit cfg id `cfg-2026-03-14-03B`.

infra-bot: cordon issued for gnode-5c. Drain in progress: 7/12 pods moved; remaining pending due to GPU scheduling constraints. Reboot scheduled once drain hits 100%.

raj: dmesg snippets: 
```
[GPU1][2026-03-14T03:04:59Z] NVRM: Xid 31:... GPU access fault
[GPU1][2026-03-14T03:05:02Z] NVRM: GPU reboot required
```
We likely need node reboot to clear driver state; also confirm whether CUDA driver v470.x has known Xid 31 regression under high prefills.

support-leah: sent transactional status to affected customers: short description, mitigation steps, ETA 02:00 for stabilized canary, will update with timeline.

ben: early canary metrics: OOM events on canary reduced by ~78%, latency increase ~0.3% for summarized-doc route. Quality check OK for now.

alice.m: live mitigation summary:
- rate-limited offending tenant and enabled route prefill truncation -> immediate drop in OOMs
- canary rollout with max_prefill_tokens=4096 (20%) and cold-fallback enabled -> fewer restarts
- streaming disabled on heavy chat route to lower concurrent KV allocations
- cordoned gnode-5c, draining and reboot planned to fix GPU driver Xid errors
- created support tickets and notified customer owners

Action items:
- @ben monitor canary and OOM/restart rate for 90m; rollback if error rate increases
- infra to reboot gnode-5c after drain completes (owner infra oncall)
- runtime (raj) to add detection/alert for single-tenant high-token floods and build temporary throttling rule
- postmortem: alice.m to open with timeline, customer impact and mitigation steps (target: 2026-03-17)

pager_sre: handoff: @ben to take pager at 04:00UTC. Alice will remain available for the handoff and overseeing reboot.

ben: taking pager. I'll post a handoff confirmation and keep monitoring memory fragmentation + Xid counts.

alice.m: filing incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incidents/1768111111 - will attach logs, canary dashboards, and customer communications. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:

pager_sre: Incident remains P1 during node reboot and canary observation window. Will move to P2 when OOM/restart rate below threshold for 30m.
